text:
anya: Heads up — noticed a reproducible drift in outputs when we do an on-the-fly quant swap + reshard. Only shows up for >32k contexts and with dynamic quant flag enabled. Minimal repro attached below.

liam: hmm, is this the same thing we've seen with rope scaling or a different symptom?

anya: different from the usual off-by-one. The token stream starts correct then after ~28k tokens it jumps to unrelated tokens — looks like a KV index aliasing issue. Happens only for sharded runs (2+ shards). Single-shard run is fine.

tom: can you paste the exact cmd you used? I'll try to reproduce locally on a 2xA100 box.

anya: sure — command: 
```
./serve --model magnet14b --shards 2 --context 65536 --quant-swap dynamic --batch 1 --streaming 
# prompt file at: https://gist.github.com/redwood/dev/repro-quant-swap-prompt.txt
```

liam: I captured a small divergence snippet — comparing expected vs actual token ids at the point of drift: 
```
EXPECTED: ... 548 12 409 77 993 14 22
ACTUAL:   ... 548 12 409 77 8412 14 22
# note: token 993 -> 8412 (completely different word)
```

dana: Does the drift align with any shard boundary or a prefill/flush event? Could be a prefill window boundary where index math uses global pos vs local pos.

anya: looks like it aligns with the moment we trigger the quant-swap (checkpoint hot-swap) after a model downgrade to int3 during throughput tests. If I avoid dynamic swapping and start with int3 from boot, no drift.

ci-bot: CI test 2918 failed on eng-ml/kv-coherence (flaky) — logging to incident tracker: https://redwood.internal/infra/issue/2918

tom: running with ROPE_VERBOSE=1 now. If it's index vs posbase mismatch, we should see misaligned rot-phase logs.

liam: small helper snippet to dump kv indices at runtime — use this before/after the swap: 
```
python tools/dump_kv.py --pid $SERVER_PID --out /tmp/kv-dump.json --range 27000-29000
# emits: [{"global_pos":..., "shard":0, "local_index":..., "rot_phase":...}, ...]
```

anya: thanks. I ran that and the dump shows duplicate local_index values across shards for the same global positions immediately after swap. Looks like the index remap step runs with stale stride metadata.

dana: suspecting the rescale code path in commit abc1234 (rotary rescale + quant metadata refactor). Can someone bisect that range?

tom: I'll bisect today on the nightly image. If I find it, I'll open a revert PR and include a test that runs the dump_kv script as a smoke.

liam: quick note — add a randomized long prompt to the unit test so we exercise actual token diversity; synthetic repeated tokens won't catch aliasing.

tom: update: bisect narrowed it to commit abc1234 -> def5678 range. The failure appears first at abc1234 which touched shard index remap + quant metadata cache. Creating PR to revert the remap change and add a guard.

anya: awesome, thanks. Can you include the failing dump and a short reproducer in the PR description? Saves us time during review.

tom: will do. PR link (draft): https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/4371

ci-bot: build 4371/1 triggered by tom — smoke tests queued.

liam: once reverted, let's add an integration that toggles quant-swap on-the-fly under a long-context streaming workload. Should be in our regression suite.

anya: agreed. Also add a check that after any hot-swap, local_index mapping sanity holds (no duplicates across shards for same global_pos).

dana: happy to own the integration test. I'll draft it with the dump_kv check and a small golden prompt set.

anya: thanks all — high priority for Dedicated customers running longsession workloads. :thumbsup:
